geometry_edits.rationale: Introduce a subtle bend so the dominant bar becomes a more legible spatial gesture rather than a pure rectangular extrusion.
Use a plan-bending axis to shape the long mass into a clearer site-responsive figure.
Apply only a small curvature so the dominant gesture remains simple and continuous.
Add a support cut on the access side to make the street response more legible and public.
Align the entry cut with the verified access side in the program frame.
Keep the cut bounded so it reads as an entry seam rather than a second courtyard.
Limit the height of the cut to preserve the dominant bar while improving ground porosity.
Use a shallow incision so the public response is legible but not over-fragmented.

graph_edits.rationale: Shift the primary mass away from a plain box toward a more articulated ribbon/bar section without losing the dominant gesture.
Narrow the bar slightly and extend it to reinforce a long horizontal datum while preserving the existing ancestry.
Add a smaller access-side entry notch/cut to strengthen the public threshold at the ground edge without replacing the protected courtyard controller.

rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent early massing diagram: a single elongated bar with a central carve/slot and a second-order split produces a readable dominant gesture and reasonable hierarchy. It responds to the parcel more as a contained linear bar than as a bounding-box filler, and the open-space figure is legible in plan and section. The access edge is acknowledged by the void, but the response remains somewhat semantically neutral rather than strongly active. The main weakness is that the section is still fairly flat and box-led, so it only partially supports the neighborhood-living brief’s need for an active ground threshold, public space, and upper hierarchy. Still, it is program-plausible and not a typology mismatch, so it passes hard fit.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is much more rectilinear and less articulated; do not copy the curved roof language.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact low-rise mass uses a large carved void and upper bridge to make a clear public threshold.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This is a much larger multi-building composition; the candidate should not become a campus complex.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Campus-like clustering around a central open space can support neighborhood program when the void stays legible.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate lacks the same richness of section and permeability.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A long low mass with a strong courtyard/atrium cut and a folded roof can support active mixed-use ground.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Avoid turning the proposal into a loose multi-wing composition; keep one dominant bar.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced, spread-out massing with connecting elements can preserve public space and hierarchy.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate should retain a simpler single-datum organization rather than multiple interlocked masses.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes with a central void and elevated connections produce a clear neighborhood threshold.

warnings: The mass is coherent but still reads close to a generic extruded bar.
Access-edge response is present but could be more clearly public and porous.
Sectional expression is modest; stronger roof/void articulation would improve program fit.
